summary: Backend-only testing for Nexus Realty FastAPI app. Created pytest suite (/app/backend/tests/test_nexus_backend.py) with 16 tests covering health, public-settings, auth (register/login/me + demo fallback + duplicate/invalid), generic entity CRUD with merge update + JSONB $in/$gt filter operators + sort/limit/skip + count + bulk create, function invoke (calculateLeadScores, checkLoanEligibility, fetchMarketData, unknown-stub), and Postgres persistence across backend restart. Found and fixed 1 critical bug: POST /api/entities/{entity}/bulk returned 422 because the route param body: Any was being interpreted by FastAPI as a query parameter (Any has no auto-body inference). After adding Body(...) annotation, all 16/16 tests pass.

minor.issue: Numeric comparisons on JSONB fields use string comparison via col.astext > str(value), so e.g. budget '90000' > '500000' is False lexically (different digit counts). Works for same-length numbers only. Consider casting to numeric or using JSONB number ops.
Returns 200 instead of 201 on resource creation (minor REST nit).
Allows arbitrary 'created_by' from request body when no auth token present (payload.get('created_by') fallback). Low risk because auth is optional by design, but worth noting.

action_items: (Optional) Improve $gt/$lt/$gte/$lte JSONB filter to cast to numeric for correct numeric comparisons (current behaviour is lexicographic on .astext).
(Optional) Return 201 from /api/auth/register and /api/entities/{entity} POST for REST correctness.
critical_code_review_comments: FIXED: /api/entities/{entity}/bulk had `body: Any` without Body(...) annotation -> FastAPI treated it as a query param and rejected all calls with 422. Added `Body(...)` so list[] and {records: [...]} payloads now work.

Numeric JSONB operators ($gt/$lt/$gte/$lte) use astext string comparison; correct only when all compared values share the same digit length. Recommend `cast(col.astext, Numeric)` or `col.as_float()` for numeric paths.
main.py auto-creates tables via Base.metadata.create_all on startup, which bypasses Alembic in dev. Acceptable for dev, but production should rely on `alembic upgrade head` and disable auto-create.
CORS configured with allow_origins=['*'] + allow_credentials=True is invalid per CORS spec; browsers will reject credentialed requests. Consider explicit origins when credentials are enabled.
auth.py: /me silently creates a demo user on first call (side-effect on GET). Functional but surprising; consider seeding via a startup task or migration instead.

entities.py to_dict in models.py spreads JSONB `data` into the response and then sets id/created_date/updated_date — any user-supplied keys named 'id', 'created_date', 'updated_date' in data would be overwritten (good), but `created_by` from data could collide with the column value (column wins only if truthy). Minor edge case.
updated_files: /app/backend/app/entities.py (added Body(...) annotation for bulk_create body param)
test_credentials: Auto-registered ephemeral users with TEST_user_<uuid>@example.com / Pass1234! per test run. Demo user demo@nexusrealty.local is auto-seeded on first /me call.
seed_data_creation: Tests create and clean up their own TEST_-prefixed entities (Lead, FilterLead, SortTest, CountTest, Property, PersistEntity).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is fully green at 16/16. If you re-run, note that test_data_survives_backend_restart issues `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` and waits up to 60s for /api/health to return 200 — keep that timeout. Bulk endpoint now expects either a raw JSON list or {records:[...]}. The /me endpoint mutates DB by creating the demo user on first call; subsequent calls reuse it.
rca of the issue: POST /api/entities/{entity}/bulk: FastAPI route handler declared `body: Any` without Body(...). FastAPI's signature inspection treats Any-typed (and other primitive/unannotated) parameters as query params, so the JSON body was never bound and the request failed validation with 422 `body field required (query)`. Fix: import `Body` from fastapi and annotate `body: Any = Body(...)`. Verified end-to-end via pytest (test_bulk_create) and curl on the external URL with both list payload and {records:[...]} dict payload.
